hero.name: Neeraj J
hero.tagline:
I'm a Data Scientist, AI Engineer, and Data Analytics professional with a Master's degree in Data Science from Florida State University. I enjoy turning complex data into intelligent products, actionable insights, and scalable solutions that create real business impact. My experience spans machine learning, generative AI, data engineering, analytics, cloud technologies, and software development, with hands-on work in Python, SQL, Spark, AWS, LLMs, and modern AI frameworks. Whether it's building end-to-end RAG systems, developing machine learning models, designing data pipelines, or uncovering insights through experimentation and analytics, I enjoy taking ownership from idea to production. I'm passionate about solving challenging problems, continuously learning, and working with teams that value innovation, curiosity, and execution. Beyond technology, I enjoy cooking, dancing, writing poetry and songs, and exploring new ideas—because I believe creativity and analytical thinking together drive the best innovations.
Always curious. Always building. Always learning. 🚀

experience.role: Center for Ocean and Atmospheric Prediction Studies
experience.description: At the Center for Ocean-Atmospheric Prediction Studies (COAPS) at Florida State University, I work as an Information Assistant developing scalable data and AI-driven systems that support oceanographic research workflows. I architected a production-grade RAG knowledge assistant using LangGraph and LangChain, integrating internal wikis, research databases, and unstructured documents into a vector search pipeline that enabled accurate natural language querying for over 50 researchers. I also engineered automated LLM-based reporting pipelines that transformed daily marine vessel records into structured summaries and trend reports, reducing manual reporting effort by 80%. In addition, I designed Python and SQL ETL pipelines processing more than 50,000 vessel records daily to power real-time dashboards and backend query systems with sub-second response times. I further modernized multiple production research websites by containerizing services with Docker, improving deployment consistency, accelerating data retrieval performance, and implementing LDAP-based access control for secure researcher access.

At Datamorphosis, I worked as a Data Engineer building scalable AI-ready data pipelines and analytics infrastructure across multiple client engagements. I developed PySpark ETL pipelines that processed and transformed more than 500K records into AWS S3 and Snowflake, enabling production-grade datasets for machine learning training and business analytics workflows. I collaborated closely with clients to design ML-focused feature schemas in dbt, translating business requirements into reliable feature tables aligned with model and product objectives. To ensure high-quality data delivery, I implemented PySpark-based validation and quality checks, including schema enforcement, null handling, and freshness monitoring. Additionally, I optimized distributed Spark SQL transformations to consistently meet performance SLAs, reduce pipeline failures, and support fast-paced experimentation workflows in production environments.

experience.company: Machine Learning Engineer and Team Lead Intern
experience.description: During my internship at Geniobits, I developed an end-to-end machine learning pipeline to identify at-risk students using academic performance data. The solution included data ingestion, preprocessing, feature engineering, model training, and evaluation, which reduced manual data preparation time by 60% and accelerated experimentation workflows across the team. I trained and optimized a PyTorch-based classification model using feature selection, cross-validation, and grid search hyperparameter tuning, achieving an F1 score of 0.82 in predicting student risk levels. To make the model accessible in production, I deployed it as a FastAPI service and built an interactive Streamlit dashboard that provided instructors with real-time risk predictions, SHAP-based model explainability, and prioritized intervention recommendations for individual students.
